title: Add or manage a BBS
instructions: Tap the gear icon at the top right of the thread picker, choose Manage BBS → Add a BBS, enter a URL, and tap Add.

title: Find a board
instructions: Tap All at the bottom to open the board list. Starred boards appear as a row of buttons at the top, with the Bulletin boards list below. If you registered several, switch with the name tabs or by swiping sideways; with only one, no tabs appear. Tap a category heading to expand or collapse it; boards are shown in three columns. Tap a board to open its thread list; go back with the back arrow or the back gesture. The board list reappears on launch and when you tap All again while it is shown.

title: Thread sorting and activity
instructions: When you open a board from All, sort tabs (Popular, New, Default) and a search button appear at the top. Popular sorts by activity: posts per day since the thread started. New sorts by newest thread. Default keeps the bulletin board's own order (threads bumped by recent posts). The search button swaps the tabs for a title search box that filters this board's thread titles on the device. It does not search other boards or threads that are not fetched yet.

title: Star a board
instructions: In the All board list, long-press a board and choose Star. Starred boards appear as rounded buttons at the top of the board list, with the most recently opened first; tap one to open it right away. To remove, long-press again and choose Unstar. Board stars do not appear in a thread's long-press menu.

title: Reading history and following threads
instructions: Threads you open are listed under Browsing at the bottom, with the number of new posts on the right. Long-press a row for Follow next thread and Delete (deleting a followed thread asks first). Followed threads gather at the top with a colored marker on the left. When a followed thread passes 900 posts, is archived, or disappears from its board's list, Gerbil looks in that board's list for a later thread with a very similar title. If found, it follows the new one, moves it to the top, and stops following the old one.

title: Reading posts and finding new ones
instructions: Threads reopen where you stopped reading. Right after opening, post-shaped placeholders appear and are replaced by the posts once the screen settles. A New posts from here line marks the post after the last one you saw. Tap New at the bottom to refresh and jump to the first new post; the bell shakes while it fetches. If nothing is new, No new posts appears at the end. The scrollbar on the right shows only while scrolling; drag it to see the post number and time. Archived threads stay readable for what was saved.

title: Post details and replies
instructions: Tap a post's header (number and time) to show the name (with wacchoi), mail, ID, and a Reply to >>N button; tap again to close. In the header, Replies n opens the replies to that post, and Posts m opens all posts by the same ID, in a sheet. Posts m turns red when the ID has posted five times or more. Tap an anchor (>>123) in the text to open that post in a sheet. Inside a sheet you can keep opening anchors and chips; the back arrow returns one level. Your own posts have their number circled.

title: Search and filter posts
instructions: Tap the search icon at the bottom of a thread to search the posts. The search ignores letter case and highlights matches. It shows n / m, and the arrows or the keyboard's search key move to the next match. The filter next to it narrows the list itself: Images & videos, Most replied (top 5 posts by replies), or Most posts (top 5 IDs by posts, showing only each person's first post). While filtering, a chip appears at the bottom; tap it to clear. Filtering does not save your reading position, and clearing returns to where you were.

title: Post or reply to a thread
instructions: Choose Post from the menu at the top right of a thread to open the post sheet. Tap a post's header and then Reply to >>N to open it with the anchor filled in. Tap the Name & mail chip to show those fields (both may be empty). Turn on sage to post without bumping the thread up the list. Your text stays as a draft until it is sent. If the bulletin board asks for confirmation, a Confirm post screen appears; check it and tap Post (or Back to edit). After you refresh, your post and posts with the same ID get their numbers circled. You can post to 2ch-compatible boards and Shitaraba.

title: Attach an image (Imgur)
instructions: Tap the image icon in the reply sheet to open the Imgur notes and Open Imgur. Open Imgur shows the Imgur page, where you upload the image. After uploading, tap COPY LINK on the Imgur screen. When you return to the reply sheet, the copied link is turned into the image's direct link and added to your post automatically. Images are stored on Imgur, not in Gerbil. Images uploaded without logging in to Imgur cannot be deleted later. Images uploaded while logged in can be deleted from your Imgur account.

title: Hide or restore posts with NG
instructions: Tap the header of a post by the person you want to hide, then tap Add to NG. If the name has a wacchoi (for example ab12-cd34), the whole wacchoi is used; otherwise the ID. Only the last four characters of a wacchoi are never used, because that would catch other people with the same phone. IDs shorter than eight characters or containing ??? are not used. NG is saved per board and applies to every thread on that board. IDs change daily, so ID entries expire after 2 days; wacchoi changes weekly, so those expire after 8 days. Hidden posts show NG · Hold to reveal and can be read only while you hold them. They are hidden in reply and ID sheets too. To undo, tap Remove from NG on a post by the same person.

title: Open links, images or the thread in a browser
instructions: Images and videos in posts show as small previews. Tap one to open it full screen; double-tap to zoom, pinch to zoom in or out, and swipe to see other images in the same post. Videos play full screen. Imgur page links are shown as the image itself. Choose how other links open in Settings → Features → How to open links: the in-app browser (a sheet from the bottom) or your browser app. Links to threads in the same format as your registered boards (/test/read.cgi/ or Shitaraba's /bbs/read.cgi/) always open in the app; links within the same thread jump to that post.

title: Appearance, fonts and text size
instructions: Change the look in Settings → Display. Appearance is System, Light, or Dark. Theme is Dynamic (wallpaper colors), a device color (Canyon, Fog, Olive, Obsidian), or a custom color that builds a palette from any color you pick. Font is System or LINE SEED JP. Post style is Modern (posts on rounded panels) or Simple (no panels). Text size is set separately from the menus at the top right of the thread list and of a thread, and also follows the system text size.

title: Glass and blur
instructions: Settings → Display → Translucency sets how floating surfaces (top bar, bottom tabs, sheets, menus) show what is behind them. Glass refracts like glass; set its refraction from 0 to 10 (default 6). Blur blurs the background; set its strength from 0 to 10 (default 6). Each surface has a fixed opacity that cannot be changed. Posts and list items never use translucency.

title: Clear the cache
instructions: Settings → Data → Clear cache deletes saved thread text, images, and summaries at once. The Browsing list, followed threads, and reading positions stay, and threads are fetched again when you open them. On supported devices, Delete local model is here too. Browsing history, saved threads, and cookies stay on this device; device backup and transfer carry over settings only.

title: Summaries and questions about a thread
instructions: On supported devices, tap the summary icon at the bottom of a thread to open the summary sheet. The on-device AI (Gemini Nano) writes the summary, and posts never leave the device. Long threads are summarized range by range, shown newest first as each range finishes. With Auto-summarize when opening a thread on (the default), it starts in the background when you open a thread. Switch the sheet to Question to ask about the thread; Gerbil picks the related posts and asks the AI once. Post numbers in the answer are kept only if they exist in the thread. If the model is missing, follow the on-screen steps to download it.

title: AI mute
instructions: On supported devices, turn on Settings → AI → AI mute (experimental), then choose Junk under Mute in a thread's filter menu. Simple rules come first: anchor-only posts, posts of only symbols like w, and identical text of 8+ characters posted 3+ times. Posts with images or videos and long posts are not judged. The rest go to the on-device AI one by one, with the replied-to text, to check against your Mute conditions (editable in Settings → AI; default: provoking posts, meaningless one-off posts, slander and personal attacks). When unsure, it does not mute. Posts nearest the screen go first, and results are saved on the device for reuse. Muted posts can be read while you hold them. Auto AI mute starts this when you open a thread.

title: Download or remove the AI model
instructions: AI features (Gerbil chat, summary, questions, AI mute) work only on devices that support Gemini Nano. AICore (a system app) manages the model and downloads about 2.7 GB in 5 to 15 minutes. It starts when you tap Download model in the on-screen guide, and keeps going after you close the app. The model may remain after you uninstall the app; delete it in Settings → Data → Delete local model. On unsupported devices, AI entry points are hidden.

title: App version and feedback
instructions: Settings → About shows the app version. Send feedback opens a form for bugs and requests. The form is filled in with the app version, device model, Android version, screen size, and display settings. Threads you read and registered boards are not sent. Choose the app language (Japanese or English) in Android's per-app language settings, not inside the app.

title: What Gerbil can do
instructions: Gerbil can do these three things. 1. Answer questions about using the app with the built-in help. 2. Find boards in the board lists of the bulletin boards you registered. 3. Find threads in thread lists already fetched; it does not search threads you have never loaded. When you name a board, it fetches that board's latest thread list to search it and can show popular threads. What it cannot do: it cannot search the internet. Your questions never leave the device.

title: Why the AI's answers are poor
instructions: Gerbil uses an on-device AI (Gemini Nano) that runs on this device. It has billions of parameters. Cloud AIs have hundreds of billions to trillions, two or three orders of magnitude more. Cloud AIs are built with thousands to tens of thousands of GPUs and use several dedicated chips to answer each question. A single phone chip is naturally much weaker.

title: Report a bug
instructions: Please send bugs and problems from Settings → About → Send feedback. The form is filled in with the app version, device model, Android version, screen size, and display settings. Threads you read and registered boards are not sent. Describing which screen you were on, what you did, and what happened makes it easier to fix.

title: The story behind Gerbil's name
instructions: The developer and his daughter went to a petting zoo and met a macaroni mouse. It was cute and friendly at first, then it suddenly bit him. That’s where Gerbil got its name. Threads can bite you out of nowhere too.
